newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan OTC market may alter share marketing system.
newsitem.headline: Japan OTC market may alter share marketing system.

text.p: The current system for selling Japanese over-the-counter (OTC) stocks, which is auction-based, may be replaced by a book-building method starting in June, stock market sources said Monday.
The Japan Securities Dealers' Association (JSDA) is currently investigating such a change, the sources said.
A final decision will be made by the JSDA after the Securities and Exchange Commission, a body advising the Finance Ministry, issues final recommendations on various deregulation issues in June.
"We are well prepared to handle the change in procedures," an official at a "Big Four" securities house said.
However, government officials said there was a chance that the recommendations may come out two or three months ahead of schedule and the book-building system could start much sooner than expected.
Under a book-building system, the price of a new share is based on information on actual investor demand gathered by the underwriter.

Under the current auction system, there is no limit on the amount of stocks an institutional investor can buy and there have been complaints that a certain investor can push up the price of a new share to unreasonable levels.
"Price determination through a book-building system will help share prices stabilise after trading starts, which could in turn increase turnover," a trader at a "Big Four" brokerage said.
Other traders said such a move could help stop sharp swings in the OTC index by preventing a situation in which new stocks with a high initial offer price fall sharply when actual trading starts.
